recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Do not restore the old TLS 1.2/cipher-suite restatement unless the Security WG makes a new current decision to restate specific IETF BCP 195 details in core FHIR.
issue_request: FHIR-15907 was a Published FHIR-core Security change request, resolved Persuasive for STU3, asking the Security page to recommend TLS 1.2 or higher for secure HTTP production data exchange, consider making that a requirement, and add strong-cipher-suite guidance.
initial_application: The request was explicitly applied in 95ee245e72, a broad Security narrative update tagged GF#15907 and GF#17242. That commit changed source/security.html from TLS/SSL wording to TLS-only production guidance, added an IETF BCP 195 paragraph, and included the requested explicit TLS 1.2-or-higher and strong-cipher-suite prose.
additional_context: FHIR-17242 was applied in the same commit and asked for BCP 195 as the TLS recommendation. FHIR-17422 later rejected a mandatory TLS 1.2 floor for core FHIR, with community discussion pointing hard version requirements to IGs or jurisdictions. FHIR-33937 is a later Published Security decision for the same paragraph; its comments/resolution favored keeping the BCP 195 reference while deleting copied TLS-version and cipher-suite details because BCP 195 changes over time.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/security.html still says production data exchange SHOULD be secured using TLS and tells implementers to follow IETF BCP 195; source/safety.html and the active safety-entries CodeSystem retain the BCP 195 checklist item.

related_jiras.note: Applied in the same 2018 Security narrative commit and explains the BCP 195 recommendation now carrying the TLS best-practice guidance.
Resolved - No Change issue rejecting a mandatory core TLS 1.2 floor, limiting FHIR-15907 to recommendation-level guidance.
Later Published issue for the same paragraph that removed stale restated TLS-version/cipher-suite details while keeping the BCP 195 reference.
